mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) compresses discount rates for equity valuations, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as the rate is a continuous predictor of equity returns.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS level shows no correlation with 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window) or 20-day returns are negative in 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS is below 0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: When unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeds 5.5%, it signals economic weakness and reduced corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: UNRATE > 5.5% occurs in 60% of cases without negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of weak GDP growth (GDPC1 below 16000 billion) and high unemployment (UNRATE above 5.5%) signals an economic downturn, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (GDPC1 < 16000 AND UNRATE > 5.5%) occurs in 60% of cases without negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS > 0.5%), the Federal Reserve's policy shift reduces liquidity and increases discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS > 0.5% occurs in 60% of cases without negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price index (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 235, it signals rising inflation and potential monetary tightening, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL > 235 occurs in 60% of cases without negative 20-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high level of housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong economic activity and consumer confidence, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days as HOUST is a continuous predictor of equity returns.
failure_condition: HOUST level shows no correlation with 20-day S&P 500 returns (Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window) or 20-day returns are negative in 60% of instances when HOUST is above 900.

mechanism_narrative: When industrial production (INDPRO) falls below 100 and payrolls (PAYEMS) fall below 139000, it signals a weakening economy and reduced corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The joint condition (INDPRO < 100 AND PAYEMS < 139000) occurs in 60% of cases without negative 60-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In a recession regime (GDPC1 below 16000 billion), weak GDP growth reduces corporate earnings and investor confidence, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 < 16000 occurs in 60% of cases without negative 5-day returns (i.e., returns are positive or flat in >40% of triggered instances) or Rank IC < 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.
